root_cause.text: The QUERY_INFO path in smb2_ioctl_query_info() failed to validate that the server-reported OutputBufferLength actually fits within the received response buffer (rsp_iov[1].iov_len) before copying data to userspace, allowing a malicious server to cause an out-of-bounds read of kernel heap memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `struct_size(qi_rsp, Buffer, qi.input_buffer_length) > rsp_iov[1].iov_len` that was missing in the original code. The vulnerability description explicitly states: "it never verifies that the flexible-array payload actually fits within rsp_iov[1].iov_len" and "A malicious server can return OutputBufferLength larger than the actual QUERY_INFO response, causing copy_to_user() to walk past the response buffer." The fix guards the copy_to_user() operation with this validation to prevent reading beyond the actual allocated response buffer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds validation to prevent buffer over-read when copying SMB2 query info response to userspace.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check before copy_to_user that validates the calculated struct size of qi_rsp with Buffer field does not exceed the actual response buffer length (rsp_iov[1].iov_len), returning -EFAULT and jumping to out label if the check fails.
intent_record.how: This prevents a potential buffer over-read when copying data to userspace. By validating that the struct_size calculation (which accounts for the variable-length Buffer field) fits within the actual allocated response buffer, it ensures copy_to_user will not read beyond valid memory bounds, preventing information disclosure or kernel crash.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the QUERY_INFO path (lines 1457-1471). At line 1460-1461, the code reads OutputBufferLength from the server response (qi_rsp->OutputBufferLength) and uses it to determine how much data to copy to userspace at line 1467. However, there is NO validation that this server-reported OutputBufferLength actually fits within the received response buffer (rsp_iov[1].iov_len). The code only compares it against qi.input_buffer_length (line 1460), but never validates it against the actual size of rsp_iov[1].iov_len. This allows a malicious server to report an OutputBufferLength larger than the actual response buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read when copy_to_user reads from qi_rsp->Buffer at line 1467. The PASSTHRU_FSCTL path has the same issue at lines 1446-1447 and 1453, where OutputCount is not validated against rsp_iov[1].iov_len before the copy_to_user at line 1453.
